title: Parameter-Shift Rules for Gradients in Boson Sampling Experiments
authors: Marius Trudeau, Pierre-Emmanuel Emeriau, Nicolás Quesada
abstract: Using a robust photon loss model for photonic quantum experiments, we derive $n-$th order parameter-shift rules for computing gradients of Fock boson sampling transition probabilities where $n$ photons are sent into a lossy interferometer. We also show that in general it is not possible to generalize this gradient recipe to the case of Gaussian boson sampling. Only in the specific case where the transmission matrix of the interferometer can be factorized as a diagonal loss matrix premultiplied by a pure unitary it is possible to obtain parameter-shift rules with a finite order given by twice the total number of photons detected. We demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed method by comparing its performance against finite differences on real hardware.
summary: This paper develops advanced Parameter-Shift Rules (PSRs) to accurately calculate gradients for boson sampling experiments operating with photon loss in integrated photonics. It provides a robust mathematical framework, showing when and how these rules can be applied to both Fock and Gaussian boson sampling regimes. The results are validated by comparing the method's performance against finite difference techniques on real hardware.
main_problem: The primary goal is deriving robust parameter-shift rules (PSRs) to compute gradients of transition probabilities in photonic boson sampling experiments that incorporate photon loss.
main_result: PSRs are derived for Fock boson sampling with a lossy model, showing limitations when generalizing to Gaussian boson sampling unless specific factorization conditions on the transmission matrix are met.
method: The authors derive PSRs by relating derivatives of observables to linear combinations of shifted function evaluations, comparing this method's performance against standard finite difference techniques.
model_or_system: The system involves bosonic modes in photonic quantum experiments, where lossy evolution is modeled by embedding the process into a larger unitary transformation acting on system and environment modes. The core mathematical tools are ladder operators and Fock/coherent states.
key_observables: Fock boson sampling transition probabilities, measurement outcome probabilities, average photon number, and photon-number correlators.
important_parameters: The order of the parameter shift rule ($n$), the total number of photons detected, and the loss parameters embedded in the transmission matrix $T$.
main_assumptions: The derivation assumes that cross-talk between modes is negligible, allowing phase-shift loss to commute with the phase shift. The method also relies on the observable being representable as a finite Fourier series.
figures_summary: Not specified in the notes; however, the text refers to figures illustrating the interferometer structure and potentially comparing PSR performance vs. FD.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the physical model of lossy evolution using an enlarged unitary transformation $W$. It then develops the mathematical framework for Parameter-Shift Rules (PSRs) applicable to this lossy setting, deriving specific rules for Fock boson sampling and analyzing the conditions under which Gaussian boson sampling can also be addressed.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the practical challenges of implementing quantum algorithms on noisy photonic hardware by providing mathematically rigorous gradient estimation techniques that outperform simple finite differencing.
